Atta's role in the 9/11 attacks was crucial, as he coordinated the hijackings and ensured that the planes were on course to their targets.

Ziad Jarrah, a 26-year-old Lebanese national, was a trained pilot who was recruited by the conspirators to pilot United Airlines Flight 93. Jarrah's plane was the fourth to hit its target, and it was intended to target the White House or the U.S. Capitol Building. Unfortunately, the passengers on the plane discovered the hijackers' plot and resisted, causing the plane to crash into a field in Pennsylvania.

The terrorists who carried out the 9/11 attacks were motivated by a desire to strike at the heart of the United States and its military power. They saw the U.S. as an oppressive force that had supported and enabled the Israeli occupation of Palestine, and they sought to draw attention to their cause by carrying out a dramatic and devastating attack.

In the aftermath of the 9/11 attacks, the world was left in shock and mourning. The attacks caused over 3,000 deaths and injured thousands more, and they had a profound impact on global politics and international relations. The terrorists who carried out the attacks may have been seen as villains by many, but their actions cannot be dismissed as senseless or random. They were motivated by a desire to challenge the status quo and to bring attention to their cause, and their actions had a significant impact on the world.
